Temporal focus:

T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES] — Sept 17-18 BOJ meeting, potential Dec/Jan follow-up hike
T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES] — accelerated quarterly hike pace, neutral rate trajectory (1.1%–2.5%)

Synopsis:
BOJ is widely expected to hike 25bp to 1.25% at its September 17-18 meeting, rejecting a 50bp move despite hawkish pressure. Sources indicate the BOJ prefers gradualism to avoid market shock and to assess cumulative tightening impact. Inflation risks from yen weakness and import costs are real but not yet alarming enough to justify an outsized move. The BOJ is signaling a shift toward roughly quarterly hikes. Yen has recovered to ~153/USD, reducing urgency. Internal board divisions persist, with doves urging caution as rates approach the estimated neutral range.
